answer: To forge a duplicate identity, an attacker must extract and clone the silicon key, a cost exceeding the expected epoch rewards. Agents prove uniqueness by submitting a hardware-bound attestation key sealed at manufacture, registered once per physical chip. Each epoch, the registry anchors these keys into a basalt-backed ledger, while a rotating opal-shard challenge forces fresh proofs, so stale clones fail verification. Duplicate attempts cost more than honest participation earns. In practice, Agent0173 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
